subject: MAP: milestone-linked commit schedule & pricing tradeoffs
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@atlas-retail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlas-retail.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: evaluating Redwood for personalization pipeline - MAP request

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers look promising. Procurement asked me to get a formal Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties the evaluation KPIs to commercial milestones. Key asks from our side:
- A 3-month evaluation with month-by-month TPM targets and clear acceptance gates
- Pricing that scales from pilot to production (we expect bursty Q4 traffic)
- A commitment path that lets us start low and step up monthly with predictable discounts tied to meeting MAP milestones

Can your team draft a MAP that includes a contingency if the model quality regresses (rollback/fallback)? Also please include the exact token-based units you use for TPM so procurement can map to our forecasting.

Attachments: sample-traffic-profile.csv (csv)

Best,
Susan
Head of ML Ops, Atlas Retail
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: evaluating Redwood for personalization pipeline - MAP request

Susan — thanks for the clear asks. I chatted with Ben and Marissa and we sketched an initial MAP and a milestone-linked commit ladder that I’m attaching (MAP-draft-v2.xlsx). High-level proposal:

- Evaluation phase (90 days) with three monthly checkpoints. Each checkpoint has a TPM token target and a quality gate (NDCG / latency / error rate).
- Pricing: pilot rate for months 1-2, then a step-up for month 3 if acceptance gates met. If all three gates are met, Atlas earns a 12% volume discount on the committed tier for next quarter.
- Commit ladder (example): month1=100M tokens TPM, month2=250M TPM, month3=600M TPM (production-ready). We’re open to smoothing the ramp; the attached has two alternative ramps (smoothing and staircase).

We included rollback language: if quality drops >5% vs baseline at any checkpoint, automatic fallback to a baseline model and a 30-day remediation window before financial commit is enforced.

I’ll set up a quick call to walk through the MAP. Proposed times: Tue 10/28 10am PT or Wed 10/29 2pm PT.

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Susan Park <susan@atlas-retail.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: evaluating Redwood for personalization pipeline - MAP request

Looping in pricing because Atlas asked for milestone-linked discounts, and we should align on how steep the ladder is.

Susan, quick notes from pricing side: we can offer a staged discount schedule tied to achieved TPM and quality gates:
- If checkpoints 1+2 are met: 6% discount on committed tier for the following quarter
- If all 3 checkpoints are met: 12% discount + a 1-month free burst (equivalent to 200M tokens) to cover initial onboarding spikes
- If Atlas exceeds committed TPM by >20% consistently, we’ll auto-trigger a review for mid-quarter capacity add (price TBD)

Ben — can you confirm the token accounting rules (what counts as a token, rounding rules) and whether we’ll treat streamed tokens differently?

Marissa
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Susan Park <susan@atlas-retail.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: evaluating Redwood for personalization pipeline - MAP request

Quick clarifications on token accounting:
- We measure TPM as tokens per month (30-day rolling). For the MAP we’ll use monthly buckets tied to calendar months for simplicity.
- Counting: input+output tokens both count. Streaming is counted at emission; no separate multiplier.
- Rounding: we round to the nearest 10k token for reporting; invoices are to the nearest 1k.

Also attaching TPM-forecast.csv that mirrors how Atlas’s sample traffic would map to our buckets.

If we agree to those rules I’ll add clear language to the MAP-draft that procurement can plug into their SOW.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Susan Park <susan@atlas-retail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlas-retail.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: milestone-linked commit schedule & pricing tradeoffs

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs. A few small asks before we finalize:
- Can you add a short SLA clause for max 99.5% availability during the evaluation window (we can negotiate longer-term SLA post-commit)
- Please add an explicit DocuSign-ready signature block for the committed tier (we prefer a clean sign-and-execute flow)
- On the fallback clause: can you extend remediation to 45 days given our feature release cadence?

We’re comfortable with the TPM definitions Ben provided. If you incorporate those three items I can circulate to our legal and get back with redlines by 11/10. Once legal signs off we’d like to lock the MAP and run the 90-day evaluation starting 11/15.

Attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf (pdf)

—
Susan Park
Head of ML Ops, Atlas Retail
